Tapping scan sweeps the local subnet with ARP requests, then reports each device\u2019s IP, MAC address, hostname and manufacturer.
Flip a device\u2019s kill switch and WiFiKill launches an ARP spoofing session, constantly re-announcing your phone as the gateway so the target\u2019s traffic is routed into a black hole.
Flip the switch off to stop the spoof and return the device to normal connectivity.
The classic network tool, revived for modern rooted Android. WiFiKill shows you who is sharing your Wi-Fi and lets you decide whether they stay. Here\u2019s the 30-second tour.
Tap scan and WiFiKill sweeps the subnet, listing every device online right now: phones, laptops, TVs, and smart-home gadgets, each with its IP, vendor, and hostname.

Flip a device\u2019s switch to cut it off. WiFiKill overrides its view of the network so the router stops talking to it, and its internet access just stops.\n\nFlip the switch back and the device is restored instantly.
Blocked clients stop streaming, syncing, and downloading, and the bandwidth they were eating goes straight back to you. Handy when someone is hogging the network mid-game or mid-call.

WiFiKill is a testing and educational tool, not a toy. Use it only on networks you own or have explicit permission to test.\n\nBlocking other people\u2019s devices without consent is disruptive and may be unlawful.
I\u2019ll only use WiFiKill on networks I own or am authorised to test
Powerful tools need deep system access. WiFiKill uses superuser (root) permissions to craft the raw network packets that scanning and blocking rely on. Ordinary apps simply can\u2019t do this.
You\u2019re all set. WiFiKill can discover and block devices on your network.

WiFiKill only works on rooted devices. If your device is rooted, open your root manager (KernelSU, Magisk, and similar), grant WiFiKill superuser access, then retry.\n\nKernelSU hides itself from apps that haven\u2019t been granted yet, so \u201Cnot granted\u201D can look exactly like \u201Cnot rooted\u201D.
Replays the welcome tour and the root check.
